name: December
editorial_article: Released in late 1982, 'December' is the fourth solo piano studio album by the American pianist George Winston. As the follow-up to his earlier 1982 release 'Winter into Spring', 'December' solidified Winston’s reputation as a cornerstone of the burgeoning New Age and ambient folk movements of the era. Recorded at Different Fur studios in San Francisco, the album serves as a poignant tribute to the winter season rather than a standard collection of holiday hits. Its success was monumental for the Windham Hill record label, helping to elevate the profile and international distribution of the label's entire catalog. \n\nThe sonic signature of 'December' is defined by Winston’s singular, minimalist approach to the piano. He strips away the ostentatious flourishes often found in classical or pop interpretations of carols, favoring a contemplative, spacious, and highly atmospheric style. Tracks like his take on Pachelbel’s Canon or the traditional 'Carol of the Bells' became hallmarks of this aesthetic, balancing stirring emotional depth with a sense of serene calm. The album proved remarkably durable, achieving triple Platinum status in the United States and remaining a fixture on the Billboard charts for years after its initial release. Its enduring legacy lies in how it bridged the gap between folk traditions, classical repertoire, and the then-emerging ambient piano scene, creating a blueprint that countless musicians have attempted to replicate in the decades since. It is a work that remains both deeply personal and universally resonant, marking a pivotal moment in the history of instrumental music. This collection of music continues to be defined by its quiet intimacy and profound emotional reach, standing as one of the most essential solo instrumental recordings ever produced, demonstrating that minimalist piano could command the attention of a massive global audience while remaining deeply rooted in folk, jazz, and classical influences. It effectively set the template for the Windham Hill sound and solidified George Winston as a key voice of American new age music.
editorial_pitch: A definitive solo piano work that redefined the seasonal holiday album, George Winston's 'December' is a masterpiece of minimalist, ambient-inflected folk piano. Mixing traditional carols with evocative originals, it stands as one of the most successful instrumental records in history.
